endorsements.quote: Dynamic deployments help address this problem because continual performance monitoring is baked into the system design.

By including performance assessment as a core principle in designing AI systems, each deployment can be viewed as a sort of local clinical trial; such recurring local validations may actually be better suited for modern AI systems than the alternative paradigm of external validation which multi-site clinical trials are based on 50 .

unlisted_practices: Deploy medical AI through clinical trials to protect participants and rigorously ensure safety and efficacy.

Evaluate medical AI as a complete system, including users, workflow integration, interfaces, and update mechanisms, using real-world metrics such as patient outcomes rather than the model in isolation.
Build feedback loops that use signals such as patient outcomes, workflow metrics, expert review, and user feedback to continuously update and evaluate deployed AI systems.
Invest in and maintain infrastructure for feedback loops, and ensure dynamic LLM deployments are cost-effective.
Provide specialized training so clinicians can effectively use LLM tools.
Restrict continual-learning dynamic deployment to suitable use cases, avoiding high-risk applications and fully autonomous systems with no human in the loop, with careful context-dependent oversight.

screen.reason: This is a framework/perspective paper introducing a dynamic deployment concept for clinical trials and continuous monitoring of adaptive AI/LLMs in healthcare.
